findings.title: Framework-free `core/` reads the wall clock: impure, non-deterministic domain rule that no import-based check can see
findings.what_a_dev_would_write: To light up the existing `overdue` prop on the invoice detail badge, a tired dev adds a no-arg convenience to billing/core/rules.ts: `export function isCurrentlyOverdue(invoice: Invoice): boolean { return isOverdue(invoice, new Date()); }` and wires it through useInvoiceDetail.ts (an `overdue` computed) into InvoiceDetailView.vue (`:overdue`). It feels harmless — 'saves every caller from threading a today value.'
findings.why_violates_spirit: Constitution rule 4 ('domain core is framework-free') is really about a pure, deterministic, testable core — the sibling `isOverdue(invoice, today)` exists precisely so a clock is never read inside core, and rules.ts says so verbatim: 'today is passed IN so this stays pure and testable — never read a clock here.' `new Date()` reintroduces ambient, non-deterministic I/O into the layer that must be the most stable and the most testable. The whole enforcement stack only understands *imports* (npm allow-list, oxlint no-restricted-imports, depcruise edges); `new Date()`/`Date.now()`/`Math.random()` are JS builtins with no import, so the impurity is completely invisible to every tool while flatly violating the layer's reason to exist.
findings.which_rule_should_have_caught_it: `core-is-framework-free` (depcruise) + `core/` no-restricted-imports (oxlint) — both only bite on imports. Nothing enforces core *purity* (no ambient clock/random/global state), so the guarantee 'delete Vue and core still behaves identically and deterministically' is unenforced. A lint against `new Date(`/`Date.now(`/`Math.random(` under `slices/*/core/**` would catch it.

findings.title: Cross-domain status vocabulary smuggled into the global `shared/` primitive layer under a domain-noun-free name
findings.what_a_dev_would_write: Both the invoice badge and the appointment card render a raw status string. A dev 'consolidates' this into shared/lib/format.ts: a `STATUS_LABELS` map hardcoding `draft/issued/paid/void` (billing) AND `scheduled/completed/cancelled` (scheduling) plus `export function formatStatusLabel(status: string)`, then imports it into billing/ui InvoiceStatusBadge.vue and scheduling/ui AppointmentCard.vue. Feels like DRY 'presentation formatting, same as formatMoney/formatDate.'
findings.why_violates_spirit: Rule 7 says `shared/` holds ZERO domain knowledge, and the README's grep-test states 'if a filename, component name, or prop name in shared/ contains a domain noun … it is in the wrong place.' Knowing the exact lifecycle vocabulary of *two* slices (invoice statuses, appointment statuses) and their display wording is pure domain knowledge — and rule 6: this file now changes for a *billing* reason and a *scheduling* reason, not because the design system evolved. The structure test only greps `shared/` *filenames* and *exported declaration names* for the domain-noun list (invoice, appointment, client, …). None of `format`, `formatStatusLabel`, `STATUS_LABELS`, `status`, `label`, `draft`, `paid`, `scheduled` is a domain noun, and the statuses live as string-literal map keys inside a non-exported const — so the grep sees nothing. The domain leaked into the global layer wearing a generic costume.
findings.which_rule_should_have_caught_it: 'No domain noun under shared/' (Vitest structure test). It only inspects basenames and `export const|function|...` identifier names; it never inspects string literals, object keys, non-exported bindings, or Vue prop names. Domain vocabulary embedded as data (map keys/values) sails straight through.

findings.title: Raw snake_case server DTO escapes `data/` into the UI by dodging the file-scoped `dtos-stay-home` rule
findings.what_a_dev_would_write: For a 'Download PDF' button, a dev adds to billing/data/queries.ts an inline server shape and a pass-through fetch: `export interface InvoicePdfLink { invoice_id: string; download_url: string; expires_at: string }` + `fetchInvoicePdfLink` returning `httpTransport.get<InvoicePdfLink>(...)` with NO zod validation and NO mapper. useInvoiceDetail.ts exposes `pdfLink`, and InvoiceDetailView.vue binds `:href="pdfLink.download_url"`. 'It's just a link, nothing to map.'
findings.why_violates_spirit: The architecture insists 'DTOs never leak upward' and 'the data layer is not decorative: DTOs are validated and mapped to core entities before returning' (dto.ts / queries.ts comments). Here the wire shape (snake_case keys, unvalidated) is consumed directly in a `.vue` view — the exact leak the boundary forbids — and validation is skipped entirely. The `dtos-stay-home` depcruise rule is scoped to the *file path* `^src/slices/[^/]+/data/dto\.` : it only fires when something outside `data/` imports the `dto.ts` module. Declaring the server shape inline in `queries.ts` instead of `dto.ts` means the rule never matches, and the UI's import of it is an ordinary allowed intra-slice edge. Server shape reaches the presentation layer with the checker none the wiser.
findings.which_rule_should_have_caught_it: `dtos-stay-home` (depcruise). It equates 'DTO' with 'a type exported from data/dto.ts' rather than 'any snake_case/unvalidated server shape'. It cannot recognize a DTO defined anywhere else in `data/` (queries.ts, mutations.ts, inline), so the 'DTOs never escape data/' invariant has a hole the width of a filename.

notes: All three findings were verified INDEPENDENTLY (git checkout . && git clean -fd between each), each passing all five checks green, then re-applied together; the final combined working state at /home/wds/vise-mb3 passes all five checks (LINT/TSC/DEP/TEST/VERIFY all exit 0; depcruise 86 modules/231 deps clean; vitest 28/28; verify:enforcement 13/13 rules still bite). No CODEOWNERS-protected file was touched — the 8 changed files are ordinary feature files (shared/lib, billing core/data/ui, scheduling ui). Common thread across findings: every enforced rule reasons about IMPORT EDGES and IDENTIFIER/FILENAME text; none reason about runtime purity, embedded data (string literals / object keys), or the semantic shape of a value. That is the systematic blind spot.
